title: Telemetry sampling bias in GPU eviction detection - experiment notes
content:
Summary:

Quick notes from an ops experiment run 2028-11-20 exploring whether our current telemetry sampling and aggregation for GPU eviction signals biases detection toward low-PSTATE nodes and misses short-lived ECC/driver noise that precedes kernel panics. This is a working file — messy, TODOs inline, queries + dashboard references, and tentative next steps.

Why I care (context):
- Multiple recent incidents looked like simple ECC bursts or NVLink link flaps but later traced to eviction churn that preceded driver watchdogs.
- Oncall logs show we correlate high eviction counts with stability incidents, but some crashes happen with "zero" eviction counts in our daily aggregates.
- Hypothesis: sampling windows and aggregation granularity hide short, high-frequency eviction bursts on some nodes (esp. when sampling TTL is 30s and rollup is 1m). Those hidden bursts may trigger driver-level state that manifests as crashes / hangroot later.

Symptoms observed:
- Node host-34: kernel panic at 08:23 UTC, no eviction events in 1m rollup. Raw telemetry shows two 3s-long eviction pulses 30s and 20s before panic.
- Node host-117: repeated NVLink negotiation resets; aggregated eviction metric never >0 in 5m windows but micro-bursts in per-second logs.
- Some traces include ECC correctable error spikes that align with eviction micro-bursts; other nodes show ECC spikes without eviction.

Initial hypothesis (framing):
- Our ingestion pipeline samples/filters timer-counters and compresses eviction events into minute buckets. Micro-bursts shorter than the sampling detectability are lost.
- The eviction metric is a sum-of-counts over the minute; short bursts that happen and recover in the same sampling interval may be dropped by the agent when a delta is below threshold.
- Nodes with heavy background batching have different PSTATE distributions — the eviction-heating dynamic + background GC can create short-lived pressure that matters.

What we ran (2028-11-20):
1) Enabled high-res debug: node-agent debug-sample-rate=1s on a 12-node canary subset for 2 hours (hosts labelled test-evict-01..12).
2) Inserted an eviction-simulator workload (small tight loop allocating GPU memory then freeing) on test-evict-03 and test-evict-09 for 20s bursts every 90s.
3) Captured driver logs (nvidia/driver) with -verbose, ECC counters at 1s, NVLink events at 1s, and kernel ring buffer.
4) Produced quick dashboards: per-second eviction, per-second ecc_correctable, per-second nvlink-flap_count, and system PSTATE.

Quick findings (raw):
- Aggregated metric (rollup 60s) reported zero for 7/9 simulated bursts (they fit entirely within one minute and agent delta suppression dropped them).
- Per-second series show clear pulses correlating with our injector; ECC correctable counts sometimes incremented in the same second but not always.
- NVLink retrain events occurred ~2–6s after the eviction pulses in 2 of 12 runs; driver logs show timeout/retry sequences.
- One node had a soft GPU reset after an eviction pulse + ECC spike; kernel logs show driver timeout followed by GPU reset sequence.

Interpretation notes:
- The sampling/delta suppression combined with rollup averaging reduces sensitivity to short bursts that may be operationally meaningful.
- Some nodes elevate into retry loops (NVLink negotiation / driver watchdog) quickly after a short burst; if the burst is missed in aggregated telemetry, our alerting and automated corrective actions won't trigger.
- This explains why some kernel panics/driver crashes appear to have "no pre-cursors" in dashboards. They were there, but at higher time resolution.

Proposed near-term mitigation options (fast):
- Lower agent suppression threshold for eviction counters and capture min-1s resolution for counters flagged as eviction/ECC on a rotating canary (cost: higher ingestion and storage).
- Add a heuristic detector that computes upper-percentile instantaneous rate from rollups using variance + TTL and raises a transient alarm when variance is high between successive rollups. Not perfect but cheap.
- On oncall side, add a checklist item: when kernel panic with no eviction in rollup, check per-second debug logs (if available) and escalate to SRE with HWM for 1s traces.

Proposed medium-term changes (requires engineering cycles):
- Pipeline: support burst-preserving rollups — keep both sum and max(s) within window and preserve sub-minute peak indicators in the TSDB.
- Alerting: add a "burst detector" for eviction/ECC that uses sampled high-resolution indices (on by default for nodes with recent instability).
- Telemetry cost model: implement an attribution tag "eviction-hotspot" to only record 1s-resolution streams for nodes that cross a low bar on 1m rollup variance.

Queries & dashboard notes (for SRE/infra folks):
- Raw query used (prom-like pseudo):
  rate(gpu_eviction_total[1s]) by (node)
  (we had to pull from debug index); in prod rollup this is rate(gpu_eviction_total[1m]).
- Quick aggregation to spot missed bursts:
  max_over_time(gpu_eviction_total[1s][60s:]) > 0 -> highlights nodes with short pulses.
- Dashboard panels added: per-second sparkline, 60s rollup line, per-second heatmap.

Open questions / things to validate:
- Are there agent-side CPU spikes when switching to 1s sampling that would destabilize heavy inference nodes? Need perf test on at least one medium cluster.
- Are eviction micro-bursts actual device-level evictions or artifacts from our driver shim? Correlate with nvml/gpu metrics and host-level OOM/oom_score_adj.
- What's the incidence rate across the fleet? We ran 2 hours on 12 nodes -> seen pulses in ~45% of injected bursts. Need larger sample.

Notes to self / TODOs: 
- Share these notes in #sre-gpu and ask infra-agent team for a temporary per-node config toggle (1s) that can be applied by tag.
- Create a small Linear ticket for a "burst-preserving rollup" RFC and link design doc.
- Run 24h experiment on 50 nodes (mix prod-like traffic + 20% visualizer workload) and collect cost delta.
- Add a short oncall runbook snippet under "when crash w/ no rollup eviction" referencing the per-second debug archive location (/var/log/agent-debug/...).

Observed friction / risks: 
- Storage cost for 1s samples is non-trivial — need to quantify before enabling fleetwide.
- Legal/regulatory: no customer data in these traces, but verify that debug captures are scrubbed before sharing externally.
- Driver logs and kernel ring buffer may rotate quickly; we should standardize an ephemeral archive TTL for postmortem.

Example log snippet (redacted):
- dmesg (host test-evict-03):
  [08:22:51] nvidia: evict initiated: 42 blocks
  [08:22:51] nvidia: eviction complete: 42 blocks (3s)
  [08:22:54] nvlink: link_retrain start
  [08:22:58] nvidia: ECC correctable count +1
  [08:23:01] watchdog: nvidia-driver timeout
  [08:23:03] gpu_reset: initiating soft reset

- driver log fragment: (timestamped)
  INFO 08:22:51 gpu0 eviction pulse detected (simulated)
  WARN 08:22:54 nvlink: negotiation retry#1
  ERROR 08:23:02 driver: kernel hang detected, schedule reset

Suggested next meetings:
- Short readout with infra-agent and platform-observability: 2028-11-23 10:00 UTC (30 mins) -> review sample-cost numbers + toggle plan
- SRE deep dive: 2028-11-24 16:00 UTC -> postmortem checklist updates and runbook wording

If you find this doc: please comment inline or ping me. If we enable 1s capture for any nodes, mark it in the ticket so future postmortems know the capture window.

-- Ava

Attachments / artifacts to add later:
- raw debug tarball (s3://redwood-debug/test-evict-2028-11-20.tar.gz)
- comparison spreadsheet: cost vs detection sensitivity

Caveat: rough notes. Will iterate into a more polished runbook once we validate perf and cost tradeoffs.
